lines: Venice is protected by a wall you can't see.
It's called MOSE. 78 steel gates lying on the seabed across the three entrances to the lagoon.
Normally, they're full of water and stay out of sight.
When a high tide is coming, air is pumped in, the water is pushed out, and the gates rise.
Construction began in 2003. On October 3rd, 2020, the gates rose for the first time and kept Venice dry.
The bill: about five and a half billion euros.
Follow for a new megaproject every day.
